name: scout-desktop
description: Microsoft Scout on a Windows PC: a PowerShell shell, the local filesystem, the public web, a browser it can drive, and the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 work data (mail, calendar, Teams, files) through WorkIQ. No accounts or credentials for other external services.

tools.bash: run PowerShell commands on Windows: scripts, CLIs, git, package installs from public registries
tools.read: read files on the local filesystem
tools.web_fetch: fetch public web pages and unauthenticated public APIs
tools.browser: drive a Microsoft Edge browser (Playwright): navigate, click, fill forms, take screenshots
tools.m365: read the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 work data through WorkIQ: mail, calendar, meetings, Teams chats, files, people
tools.teams_message: send a Teams message as the signed-in user
tools.azure_devops_mcp: read and update Azure DevOps work items, repos and pipelines the user can access
tools.ask_user: ask the user a question and read the answer in the conversation
tools.windows_os: Windows itself: winget, Windows apps and the Windows App SDK

lacks: accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the user's Microsoft 365 work account (cloud providers such as AWS, app stores, Expo, Hugging Face, Cloudflare, payment)
macOS or Linux, and their toolchains (Xcode, CocoaPods)
publishing packages, apps or sites to any public hosted service
